name: The Lamb household at 2011 Prairie Avenue
head: pa1904_lamb_augustus_d

present_on_scene_date.note: Listed at 2011 Prairie Avenue in the Blue Book for 1904 (canvass begun September 1903) and again in the 1905 edition (canvass begun September 1904), which bracket 1 July 1904. The 1905 list prints: 2011 Augustus D. Lamb; Benjamin B. Lamb.

associated_with.note: The Blue Book's Prairie Avenue street list prints the household at 2011, and the 1905 list again. The book gives no date the household came or went, so neither end is dated here.

not_in_this_household.note: WHO IS NOT ON THIS CARD, AND WHY. The Blue Book is a society register: it names the family members who received and were received, prints unmarried daughters only as '& dr.', and names no young children, servants, coachmen, cooks or nurses. The 1900 census (ED 40, T623 roll 245) was read for this card. The three live-in staff it lists at the house on 1 June 1900 are on the card, graded inferred because the count was taken four years before the scene. The 1910 census was not read. A person goes on this card when a source names them, and not before.

persons.name: Augustus D. Lamb
persons.note: Listed first of the two Lambs at 2011; the Blue Book does not say who headed the house, and the card is anchored on the first name. The 1900 census lists A. D. Lamb here as father, born April 1825 (the figures are hard to read), in Pennsylvania, widowed (ED 40, sheet 12A, line 37, leaf n816).

persons.name: Benjamin B. Lamb
persons.note: Listed at 2011 in both editions. The Blue Book does not say how the two Lambs were related. The 1900 census lists B. B. Lamb here as head, born January 1860, in Illinois, single (ED 40, sheet 12A, line 36, leaf n816).

persons.name: Ida Johnson

born.note: The census gives April 1865, age 35 on 1 June 1900.

occupation.note: Written as "Waitress" in the occupation column on 1 June 1900.

persons.note: Enumerated on 1 June 1900 in the house, as a servant (waitress); born April 1865, in Sweden, came to the United States in 1887, single. Servants changed places often, so this records who worked here in 1900; no source read says whether this person was still here on 1 July 1904.
